First, note that

$$
\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{10}}={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-10}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-10$ and $\phi =\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{10}} & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-10} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-10\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-10\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(-10\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-10\theta )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(10\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(10\theta ).
$$
